input.quote: 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
input.rationale: § 12.4 (p0045) is the only non-solicit in the document and it is one-way against Customer: it bars soliciting, hiring or employing any Vendor employee (not just personnel involved in the Services) for the term plus 24 months, with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out ("regardless of how the employee applies"). That is a no-hire covering all Vendor personnel at the outer duration limit — walk-away territory and a clear failure of the fallback on every element. It also contradicts § 12.3 (p0044), in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no no-hire commitment and is free to hire anyone responding to general recruitment. We therefore take the preferred position and remove the restriction on Customer with a single edit to the prohibitory operator and duration; the fallback (mutual, solicitation-only, involved personnel, 12 months, with carve-outs) is offered in the comment.

ops.oldText: Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.
ops.newText: Customer is subject to no restriction on soliciting, hiring, or employing any Vendor employee.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept non-solicitation or no-hire restrictions on Customer, and this one-way clause covers all Vendor employees for 24 months with no general-advertising or unsolicited-applicant carve-out and contradicts § 12.3. We have removed the restriction; as a fallback we could accept a mutual, solicitation-only restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months with those carve-outs.
proposal.summary: Remove the Customer non-solicit/no-hire restriction in 12.4
